alt: “So-called solution”: the modifier both qualifies the noun and conveys the writer’s doubt. A table shows six more modifiers, from “a modest proposal” to “the regrettably necessary cuts”, with what each modifies and the attitude it conveys.
caption: Read modifiers for attitude, and choose them for attitude.

alt: Five vague sentences replaced by precise ones, such as “The meeting was bad” becoming “The meeting ran two hours and ended without a decision”. Below, three habits: replace vague words, prefer strong verbs to verb plus adverb, and use concrete nouns and numbers.
caption: Precision reduces confusion; the exact word is often a plain one.

alt: Two boxes: a verdict, “The policy failed”, in which the writer has judged; and information, “The policy reduced waiting times by a minute but raised costs by a tenth”, which trusts the reader to judge.
caption: A verdict tells readers what to think; precise information lets them judge.

alt: Lincoln’s sentence with its modifiers labelled: the adverbs “fondly”, “fervently” and “speedily”, and “mighty scourge” presenting war as a force of punishment. Below, Paine’s “summer soldier and the sunshine patriot”, where two nouns used as modifiers carry a judgement about fair-weather loyalty.
caption: Short, well-placed modifiers can carry feeling, judgement and argument.

after: ## Worked example 1: making a draft precise
alt: Five vague phrases from the pool draft mapped to precise details: “bad state” to “falling apart”, “not nice” to cracked floor tiles, “a lot of things broken” to two of six showers not working, “problems” to a fallen ceiling tile, and “very unpleasant” to a swimmer slipping on the dangerously wet floor.
caption: Replace vague words with what you actually know, then add a modifier only where it helps.

after: ## Worked example 2: analysing modifiers and precise words
alt: The brochure passage with modifiers highlighted in cream (sleek, bold, blandly, Quietly) and exact details in teal (40 new jobs, page nine, the fishermen’s slipway). Notes explain that the modifiers signal distrust and the details give that distrust a basis.
caption: Sceptical modifiers signal the attitude; exact details let the reader share it.
